name: Klaus-Dieter Ziegler
bio:
Klaus-Dieter Ziegler's motorsport journey began unexpectedly. Initially trained as a mechanical engineer, he found his meticulous approach and analytical mind were better suited to trackside strategy than wrenching on engines. He started in Formula Ford, quickly gaining a reputation for his uncanny ability to predict pit stop windows and capitalize on track conditions. He transitioned to GT racing a decade ago, developing a knack for maximizing a team's strengths and mitigating their weaknesses. 

Klaus's approach is data-driven, but he also trusts his gut. He studies weather patterns, tire degradation, and competitor tendencies relentlessly, building a comprehensive picture that informs his decisions. He is known for his calm demeanor under pressure, his ability to communicate complex information clearly, and his unwavering focus on the big picture. What sets Klaus apart is his willingness to challenge conventional wisdom, often devising unconventional strategies that catch opponents off guard.

physical.description: A man of medium build, he often wears frameless glasses perched on his nose.

quirks: Always carries a small notebook filled with handwritten calculations.
Has a strong preference for black coffee, consuming several cups throughout a race weekend.
Refuses to make a strategy call without first consulting a specific vintage weather app on his phone.
